# A pair list defines a perfect matching

**Claim.** If the flattened endpoints of a pair list are a repetition-free permutation of a list containing every vertex, then the graph generated by the pairs is a perfect matching, also when regarded as a subgraph of any graph containing it.

**Proof.** The permutation hypothesis transfers the absence of repetitions from the vertex list to the flattened endpoint list. Since that flattening is made from the two endpoints of each pair, its lack of repetitions implies both that each pair has distinct endpoints and that endpoint lists belonging to distinct pairs are disjoint.

Take any vertex $u$. It occurs in the vertex list, hence in the flattened endpoint list by the permutation hypothesis. Thus it is one endpoint of some listed pair $(a,b)$. The pair has distinct endpoints, so it supplies an edge from $u$ to its other endpoint. This edge is present in the generated graph by the adjacency characterization (`pairListGraph_adj_iff`).

That neighbor is unique. If another generated edge joins $u$ to $w$, the same characterization says that some listed pair contains those endpoints in one of the two orientations. If it were a different pair from the one containing $u$, their endpoint lists would intersect at $u$, contradicting the disjointness just established. If it is the same pair, its other endpoint must be the already chosen neighbor. Thus every vertex has exactly one neighbor in the generated graph, which is the perfect-matching condition. The assumed subgraph inclusion lets this generated graph be regarded as a subgraph of $G`; the argument establishes the matching property for that subgraph.

**Key facts.** `FABL.pairListGraph_adj_iff`.
